This game could have easily been named 'Tamiya Model Simuator.' 

You will not be diagnosing electrical problems, tuning engines, or fixing broken suspension. You will tear vintage tanks down to to their bare hulls, rebuild them with new or refurbished pieces, and wave magic wand tools over them to simulate repair and painting. Your reward will be a tank you can drive, put on display, or sell for a profit.

I have now completed eleven tanks including four for my museum. The M4 Sherman drivetrains are insanely detailed and have seemingly endless gears, bearings and pins. I spent over three hours last night completely restoring an M4 'Easy Eight' Sherman pulled from the scrapyard. I have a rusted hull of a Tiger I sitting in the workshop for this weekend.

Rebuilding the tanks is addictive. Unfortunately, the initial tutorial is trash. Check out the community guides before you begin your first project.

I failed my first build because I didn't understand how to manage the workflow. I kept buying completely new parts as I went along, for a tank that came in already half-restored. I quickly burned through $8,000 cash and a $20,000 bank loan (before interest) working on a contract worth a maximum $18,000 payout. I tried to complete the contract before it was fully completed, and was warned of a $5,000 penalty. So I started the game over and learned from the community guides.
